template.title: Project-Aware Work Summary Template
template.purpose: Guide the creation of a durable Markdown source document that preserves the project context, narrative of the work, technical evidence, project-state change, audience-specific views, and publication material for one documented body of work.
template.documentRole: The generated summary.md is the authoritative narrative source for the work update. The public HTML document, sidecar JSON, project delta, supervisor email, image brief, listing description, and other publication artifacts are derived from it.
notIntendedToBe: a replacement for the complete project record
a replacement for the documentation workflow specification
a complete copy of the sidecar schema

currentConversation.purpose: Recover the actual work, reasoning, decisions, errors, tests, and outcomes.

primaryProjectRecord.purpose: Establish the durable project goal, scope, parent relationship, and current state.

primaryProjectRoadmap.purpose: Reconcile completed work against prior open work and revise the still-to-do list.

recentProjectUpdates.purpose: Preserve continuity and identify previous state, unresolved work, and direction changes.

relatedProjectRecords.purpose: Explain cross-project effects, dependencies, and shared foundations.

workFiles.purpose: Confirm filenames, components, data structures, scripts, and artifacts.

screenshotsAndImages.purpose: Support interface, visual, and publication claims.

testsAndVerificationResults.purpose: Separate implemented and verified work from planned or discussed work.

deploymentAndPublicationInformation.purpose: Record canonical URLs, deployment status, and publication readiness.

missingContextBehavior.projectRecordUnavailable: Infer the probable project context cautiously from the available work evidence. Label the conclusion as provisional and do not invent a stable project ID.
missingContextBehavior.roadmapUnavailable: State that no prior roadmap was available. Do not invent earlier outstanding work.
missingContextBehavior.relatedProjectRecordUnavailable: Describe the observed relationship without presenting the related project's broader state or goals as known.
missingContextBehavior.verificationUnavailable: Distinguish work described or implemented from work actually tested or observed.
missingContextBehavior.canonicalUrlUnavailable: Record the URL as still needed rather than guessing or copying a temporary runtime URL.

sections.heading: Document Identity
sections.purpose: Identify the body of work and provide stable processing information.
questionsToAnswer: What is this summary called?
What date or work period does it cover?
What is the primary project, if known?
What documentation run or source conversation does it belong to?

outputGuidance.format: short metadata block or compact introductory lines
avoid: long narrative
duplicate title information already present in YAML front matter

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.purpose: Provide a concise account of what the work was, why it mattered, and what changed.
questionsToAnswer: What body of work was completed or advanced?
What problem or goal prompted it?
What was the principal result?
What remains unfinished or uncertain?

avoid: implementation minutiae
unsupported claims of completion
mere chronology without significance

sections.heading: Project Context
sections.purpose: Explain the durable undertaking that gives the work its meaning.
questionsToAnswer: What is the primary project?
What parent project or umbrella program contains it?
What is the project's durable goal?
What phase or condition was the project in before this work?
Which applications, releases, components, or shared foundations are involved?
What prior work or roadmap established the starting context?
How confident is the project identification?

outputGuidance.format: structured subsections followed by concise explanation

sections.heading: Situation Before the Work
sections.purpose: Establish the problem, condition, limitation, or opportunity that existed before the work began.
questionsToAnswer: What was true before this body of work?
What problem or limitation presented itself?
What evidence showed that work was needed?
What assumptions or expectations existed at the start?

avoid: retelling the final solution prematurely
describing the initial state using knowledge learned only afterward without noting the hindsight

sections.heading: Narrative of the Work
sections.purpose: Preserve how the problem, investigation, construction, decisions, and final approach actually developed, including the method by which the result was reached.
questionsToAnswer: What situation prompted the work?
How was the problem initially understood?
What outcome was intended?
What approach was chosen and why?
What happened as the work progressed?
What evidence changed the understanding of the problem?
What failed, proved misleading, or required revision?
What turning points altered the direction?
How did the final approach emerge?
What method or reusable rule was established?
What did the work teach us?

avoid: mere task lists
false appearance that the solution was inevitable
removing uncertainty that materially shaped the work

sections.heading: Work Performed
sections.purpose: Provide a precise accounting of the actions, artifacts, files, features, and changes involved.
questionsToAnswer: What was created, changed, removed, tested, deployed, or documented?
Which files, services, data stores, interfaces, or records were affected?
Which work items were completed versus merely discussed?
What concrete artifacts now exist?

outputGuidance.format: organized subsections and lists where useful
outputGuidance.filenameSpecificity: include exact filenames when known and materially useful
avoid: claiming implementation when only planning occurred
duplicating the entire narrative

sections.heading: Decisions and Design Reasoning
sections.required: when decisions materially shaped the work
sections.purpose: Preserve important choices, alternatives, reasons, and consequences.
questionsToAnswer: What important decisions were made?
Why was each decision made?
What alternatives were considered?
What tradeoffs or consequences followed?
Did any decision change the project's direction or architecture?

avoid: inventing alternatives that were not discussed
presenting later outcomes as the original reason

sections.heading: Problems, Wrong Turns, and Resolutions
sections.purpose: Record failures, misleading symptoms, rejected approaches, and how they were resolved.
questionsToAnswer: What problems were encountered?
What effect did they have?
Which attempted approaches did not work?
Why were those approaches reasonable at the time?
What evidence showed they were wrong or insufficient?
How was each problem resolved or left unresolved?
What was learned from the failure?

outputGuidance.format: problem-resolution entries or short narrative subsections
avoid: blaming language
excessive low-value detail that does not aid future reconstruction

sections.heading: Verification and Evidence
sections.purpose: State what supports the account and distinguish verified results from assumptions or plans.
questionsToAnswer: What tests were performed?
What results were observed?
What screenshots, files, logs, outputs, or records support the claims?
What deployments or interfaces were verified?
Which claims remain unverified?
Were any regressions or failure cases checked?

avoid: using 'working' without describing the evidence
implying successful testing from code inspection alone

sections.heading: Resulting Capabilities and Current State
sections.purpose: Describe what is now possible and the exact condition of the work after the documented session.
questionsToAnswer: What capabilities now exist?
What is the current operational or development status?
What is stable, experimental, beta, incomplete, or unavailable?
What practical difference does the result make?
What limitations remain?

outputGuidance.format: plain-language state description with technical detail where needed
avoid: confusing completed code with a completed project
omitting beta or experimental status

sections.heading: Project Delta and Roadmap Reconciliation
sections.purpose: Explain exactly how the project state and roadmap changed because of this work.
questionsToAnswer: What was the previous project state?
Which prior roadmap items were completed?
Which were partially completed?
Which remain open?
Which were deferred?
Which were superseded or made unnecessary?
What new work was discovered?
What is the resulting project state?
What is the revised ordered still-to-do list?

outputGuidance.format: explicit status categories followed by a revised roadmap

sections.heading: Related Projects and Shared Systems
sections.required: when the work materially touches another project, component, or foundation
sections.purpose: Explain cross-project effects rather than merely listing affected apps.
questionsToAnswer: What other projects were affected?
How was each related project affected?
Was the relationship functional, technical, informational, visual, operational, or infrastructural?
What shared data, services, directories, or foundations were used?
Did the work create or change a dependency?
Did another project receive a new capability, obligation, or risk?

outputGuidance.format: one subsection per related project or shared foundation
avoid: treating all affected applications as equal project memberships
asserting the state of a related project without evidence

sections.heading: Knowledge Produced
sections.required: when the work produced reusable knowledge
sections.purpose: Identify lessons, recurring problems, rules, and possible knowledge-base additions.
questionsToAnswer: What project-specific lessons were learned?
What lessons apply across projects?
Was a recurring problem recognized?
Was an existing rule confirmed, revised, or contradicted?
Should any lesson become a permanent knowledge-base article or development rule?
What evidence supports promoting the lesson?

avoid: turning one incident into a general rule without support

sections.heading: Supervisor View
sections.required: for published work updates intended for supervisor review
sections.purpose: Create the plain-language material for the supervisor reading path, callouts, and email.
questionsToAnswer: What changed in plain language?
Why does it matter operationally?
What is the current status?
Is any action, approval, decision, or testing required?
What risks or limitations should a supervisor know?
What would staff notice?
What is the next operational step?
Which points deserve separate supervisor callouts in the HTML?

sections.heading: Publication Material
sections.required: when the summary will produce public or internal publication artifacts
sections.purpose: Collect canonical reusable text and visual direction for later publication products.
questionsToAnswer: What should the work-update headline be?
What short listing description should appear in an index or portal?
What should the supervisor email subject and body say?
What should the work-update image communicate?
What alt text should describe the image?
Which canonical URLs exist and which are still needed?

avoid: independently rewriting contradictory summaries for each destination
using temporary Apps Script runtime URLs as canonical URLs

downstreamUses: Google Sites or generated index listing

sections.heading: Files, Resources, and References
sections.purpose: Identify the artifacts needed to continue, verify, publish, or reconstruct the work.
questionsToAnswer: Which source files were created or changed?
Which spreadsheets, repositories, applications, services, or documents were involved?
What are the canonical public or deployed URLs?
Which resources are historical, temporary, replaced, or still unknown?
Where should a future conversation look first?

avoid: inventing repository paths
presenting unresolved URLs as final

sections.heading: Uncertainties and Unresolved Questions
sections.purpose: Preserve ambiguity, missing evidence, provisional interpretations, and questions for later work.
questionsToAnswer: What remains uncertain?
Which conclusions are inferred rather than explicit?
What evidence is missing?
What project relationships remain provisional?
What decisions or validations are still needed?
What should the next conversation verify first?

avoid: hiding uncertainty to make the document appear complete

conditionalRules.condition: technical files, scripts, schemas, or code were changed
conditionalRules.requireDetail: exact filenames when known and materially useful

conditionalRules.condition: a decision materially changed architecture, scope, or workflow
a failed or misleading approach affected the final method
the work affects another durable project
the work produced reusable or recurring knowledge
the update is intended for supervisor review
the update will be published or emailed
an Apps Script application was deployed or modified

conditionalRules.requirePublicationField: image concept, repository path when known, URL when known, and alt text

conditionalRules.condition: project records do not yet exist
conditionalRules.behavior: Use provisional project context and explicitly record the missing project record.

qualityChecks.question: Does the summary explain what situation or problem prompted the work?
Does the summary preserve how the solution or method emerged rather than only listing the final result?
Are chronology and causal relationships clear where they matter?
Are explicit facts, observations, inferences, and unknowns properly distinguished?
Does the summary distinguish completed, partially completed, planned, discussed, deferred, and superseded work?
Are claims of success supported by tests, observations, files, screenshots, or deployment evidence?
Does the summary explain the primary project and its goal without confusing the project with an app version or component?
Does the summary reconcile the previous roadmap and produce a revised still-to-do list?
Are related-project effects explained rather than merely named?
Can a supervisor understand the operational significance, status, limitations, and required action?
Are the supervisor callouts ordered and suitable for a jump-linked skim path through the HTML?
Can the HTML, sidecar, email, image brief, and listing description be generated without rereading the whole conversation?
Can a future conversation use the summary to understand where the project stands and what to do next?
Are unresolved questions and missing evidence recorded rather than silently filled?
